summary: Process switch `implementation_schedule` lets the implementation roles of one Delivery Item write in parallel lanes. `sequential_v1`, the default, keeps today's order and every compiler output, and an Item without the field reads as `sequential_v1`. At `parallel_lanes_v1`, `delivery_compile.py init` writes `implementation_schedule`, `lane_scopes` (`<role>:<path>`) and `lane_seams` (`<producer> -> <consumer> via <interface>`) on each new Item with two or more implementation roles besides the Software Architect. `approve-execution` requires scopes that are disjoint in both directions, together equal `path_claims`, stay out of `workspace/docs`, `.git` and `.agentrof`, and cover every implementation role except the Software Architect; seams that join two lanes, name a claimed contract or an architecture record of a claimed kind and form no cycle; and a Process Policy that still selects the schedule. The Execution Plan renders the Software Architect alone, the lanes in seam order, then Code Review and QA, and the Item and plan hashes cover the lane plan. `task_inputs.py` bounds a lane role's write scope to its lane, while the Item keeps one worktree, Item ref, Slot and writer receipt epoch and the coordinator stays the only committer. Switch references for execution planning and Delivery execution carry the lane rules: a code-level seam specification before lanes start, no Git writes by a lane except `git add -N` for its own new files, cross-lane requests through the coordinator, isolated test environments, serial environment verbs and one commit before the freeze.
